title: Help Emily Fight Her Brain Tumor
description: Emily, 21, has been diagnosed with a grade IV glioblastoma (GBM) — the most aggressive malignant brain tumor. She urgently needs dendritic cell immunotherapy in Germany — a treatment not covered by any insurance in the United States.

story.intro: Emily is a 21-year-old pre-med student at Boston University who was diagnosed with Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM), WHO grade IV — the most aggressive malignant brain tumor. Standard treatment (surgery, radiation, temozolomide) offers a median survival of just 14-16 months. The only therapy that could significantly extend her survival — dendritic cell immunotherapy — is available only at specialized centers in Germany and is not covered by any insurance plan in the United States.

sections.title: The Diagnosis
sections.content:
It all started in October 2025, when Emily began experiencing persistent morning headaches accompanied by nausea and blurred vision in her left eye. On October 20th, after a seizure during a lecture at Boston University's pre-med program, she was rushed to the Neurosurgery Department at Massachusetts General Hospital.

The MRI revealed a 4.2 cm mass in her right frontal lobe with characteristic ring enhancement and perilesional edema. Stereotactic biopsy and molecular analysis confirmed the diagnosis: Glioblastoma Multiforme, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade IV, with unmethylated MGMT promoter — the most unfavorable molecular subtype, meaning reduced response to chemotherapy.

sections.title: Standard Treatment and Its Limits
sections.content:
Emily underwent partial surgical resection (subtotal resection) on November 5, 2025 at Mass General — complete removal was not possible due to the tumor's proximity to functional speech areas. She then followed the Stupp protocol: concurrent radiotherapy (30 sessions over 6 weeks) with daily temozolomide, followed by maintenance temozolomide cycles.

Her doctors were honest: with unmethylated MGMT, response to temozolomide is expected to be limited. Median survival with standard treatment is 12-15 months. The follow-up MRI in January 2026 showed residual tumor stable in size, but her doctors warned that recurrence is almost certain.

sections.title: The Hope: Dendritic Cell Immunotherapy
sections.content:
After extensive research, Emily's family identified a specialized dendritic cell immunotherapy program at a certified oncology center in Germany. A recent clinical study (Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics, 2025) demonstrated a 68% increase in median overall survival for glioblastoma patients who received dendritic cell vaccines.

The therapy works as follows: cells are harvested from Emily's blood, converted into dendritic cells in the laboratory, 'trained' with antigens from her own tumor, and reinfused to activate her immune system against the cancer. 4-6 cycles are required over 12 months.

This therapy is NOT covered by any insurance plan in the United States — not Medicare, not Medicaid, not any private insurer. It is classified as 'experimental' by the FDA and is available only on a private-pay basis at specialized centers in Germany.

sections.title: Why We Need Your Help
sections.content: We want to be completely transparent. Emily's standard treatment at Mass General was covered by her family's insurance (with significant copays and deductibles already totaling over $18,000). What we're asking for is exclusively for treatments that no insurance in America will cover — but that could give Emily a real chance at life beyond the 14-month standard prognosis.

quote.text: I wanted to become a doctor to help people. Now I'm learning what it means to be a patient — and how unbearable it is to know that a treatment exists that could save you, but you can't access it. Every donation isn't just money — it's time. Time I get to keep living. If I make it through this, I promise to dedicate my life to neuro-oncology, so no one else has to go through what I'm going through.
quote.author: Emily R.

updates.title: Follow-up MRI results are in 📋
updates.content: The follow-up MRI after completing radiation shows stable residual tumor with no new lesions. Her doctors at Mass General say this is the best possible outcome with standard treatment, but recurrence remains very likely. The clinic in Germany has confirmed they can begin dendritic cell therapy in April, if we secure the funding.

updates.title: We've passed 600 donors! 🙏
updates.content: Your support has been overwhelming. Emily has finished her maintenance temozolomide cycles and is feeling strong. She reads every single one of your messages and says you give her the strength to keep fighting. Every dollar brings us closer to Germany.

updates.title: Treatment update
updates.content: Emily has completed concurrent chemoradiation at Mass General. She experienced fatigue and nausea, but her mental strength is incredible. Her neuro-oncologist explained that with unmethylated MGMT, temozolomide alone isn't enough — which is why immunotherapy is critical.

updates.title: The campaign has launched
updates.content: With heavy hearts but determination, we're launching this appeal. After three months of intensive treatment through the standard care system, her doctors told us clearly: standard treatment buys time, but immunotherapy can give her a life. Unfortunately, it's not covered by any insurance in the US. We believe in the power of community.
